title: Clopen diagonal and degree-one criterion for etale maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $a:U\to X$ be separated and etale. Its diagonal $U\to U\times_XU$ is both an open immersion and a closed immersion, so it has an open and closed complement. If $a$ is surjective on point classes and every geometric fibre has exactly one point, then $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), etale diagonal; Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open), with Tag 040X (lemma-universally-injective).

proof.text: Put $W=U\times_XU$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and let $\delta:U\to W$ be the diagonal. By [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests], $\delta$ is representable and a monomorphism: after every scheme test its source is a scheme and its map is monic. This also proves monicity as a sheaf map, since on a test scheme a point of the diagonal over $(u_1,u_2)$ exists precisely when $u_1=u_2$, and then is unique. Composition of representable etale maps in [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] shows that $a$ composed with every representable etale scheme chart is representable etale. Thus $a$ is chartwise etale. By [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], $p_1$ is chartwise etale by base change, and $a p_1:W\to X$ is chartwise etale by composition. Apply its comparison clause to $U\to X$, $W\to X$, and $\delta$ over $X$: $\delta$ is chartwise etale. Thus [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] makes $\delta$ an open immersion. Separatedness of $a$, as defined in the statement, makes this same diagonal a closed immersion on scheme tests.

Identify $U$ with the open subspace $D\subseteq W$ given by $\delta$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], its underlying subset pulls back on any scheme atlas $T\to W$ to the underlying open of $D\times_WT$. This scheme-test immersion is also closed by separatedness, so that open subset of $T$ is closed. The atlas-topology definition [def-a1-space-point-topology] therefore makes $|D|$ closed as well as open in $|W|$. The open-subspace correspondence of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] supplies the complementary open subspace $C$ with $|C|=|W|\setminus|D|$. On each scheme test, $C$ is the open subscheme complementary to the clopen subscheme $D\times_WT$. Its inclusion is a closed immersion too: its image is closed and the restriction map of structure sheaves is surjective on stalks (an isomorphism on $C$, and a map to the zero stalk off $C$). Hence the complement is open and closed, with its induced structure.

source.place: Tags 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces) and 03BX (lemma-topology-points), applied to the clopen diagonal.

proof.text: Now assume the geometric-fibre hypothesis. For any algebraically closed $\Omega$ and $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, representable etaleness in [def-trf-algebraic-space] says that $F_x=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a scheme etale over $\Omega$. It is therefore unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] to this scheme over the field $\Omega$: it is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $\Omega$. Every such extension equals $\Omega$: the minimal polynomial of an element is irreducible, and over an algebraically closed field an irreducible polynomial has degree one. Exactly one underlying point therefore means exactly one summand, and $F_x\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ over $\Omega$. In particular it has a unique $\Omega$-section.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), part (1), applied to the geometric fibre.

proof.text: Every point class of $W$ has a representative $z:\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ by [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Choose an algebraic closure $K\hookrightarrow\Omega$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Write $z_\Omega=(u_1,u_2)$, so $a u_1=a u_2=x$. Each $u_i$ is a section of the same $F_x\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, hence Step 3 gives $u_1=u_2$. Thus $z_\Omega=\delta u_1$. The representative $z$ and its extension $z_\Omega$ define the same point class, so every class lies in the image of $|\delta|$. This is surjectivity on point classes of the diagonal, not merely injectivity on the point classes of $a$.

source.place: Tag 040X (lemma-universally-injective), diagonal-surjectivity argument, using the geometric fibre calculation of Step 3.

proof.text: The open subspace $D\subseteq W$ of Step 2 has full point image by Step 4. The final clause of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $D=W$. Consequently $\delta$ is an isomorphism. For any scheme $T$ and $u,v\in U(T)$ with $a(u)=a(v)$, the pair $(u,v)\in W(T)$ has a preimage under $\delta(T)$; both its projections equal that preimage, so $u=v$. Thus $a$ is a monomorphism of sheaves on every test scheme, including nonreduced ones.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] to $a$, which is etale by hypothesis and monic by Step 5. It identifies $U$ with an open subspace $J\subseteq X$. The assumed surjectivity on point classes makes $|J|=|X|$. The full-image clause of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $J=X$, and hence $a$ is an isomorphism.

tool_uses.why: Generic representability and monicity of relative diagonals; the unit does not replace the foundational scheme-test argument.
Generic base change, composition and comparison calculus for etale maps of algebraic spaces, used to show that the diagonal is etale.
Generic point-image and open-subspace calculus, including that a full-image open subspace is the whole space.
Only its open-subspace/open-subset correspondence is used to construct the complement.
Generic scheme-over-field decomposition, applied to a represented geometric fibre; no unit-level finiteness argument is replaced.
Generic representable etale composition, used only to pass from the stated scheme-test etaleness to chartwise etaleness.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q24-4f705f530 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, the parent's d=1 use in lem-sfb-qcqs-space-integral-scheme-cover, all 13 cited statements, and Stacks 05W1, 05W5, 040X, 03HK and 02G7 at the cited places. The statement is unchanged, has no new nodes and is true: it is the 05W1 open diagonal plus the 05W5/040X criterion.

Steps:
- Step 1: the diagonal is representable and monic, then chartwise etale by base change, composition and comparison, so it is an open immersion. 'Etale on scheme charts' in the etale-monomorphism node is the 03FR notion, and chartwise etale plus representable gives representable etale, so this is not a gap.
- Step 2: inverse-image clause and final topology give a clopen |D|, and the complement subspace is a closed immersion. OK.
- Step 3: by 02G7 and algebraic closedness, a singleton fibre is Spec Ω with a unique section. OK.
- Step 4: the Ω-extension argument shows |δ| is surjective. OK.
- Steps 5-6: an open subspace with full image is the whole space, then the monomorphism and full image give the isomorphism. OK.

Small cases checked: empty space, X⊔X, an open inclusion, nontrivial separable L/k, and inseparable extensions.

The six declared tool_uses are generic algebraic-space foundations and are accepted. Batch-5: all eight flagged citations are general definitions or foundations (03HK, 03FT-03FV, 03EC, 05W5, 03H4/03BX/03BZ, 02G7, 03BU), not trace-formula or Poincaré-duality steps; no RETURN. No SGA source is used.
